item.title: California moves to exempt Linux from its age-verification law after backlash
item.description:
📝 Critics argued the law’s wording was so broad that it could technically force open-source operating systems to become age-verification platforms. Linux developers also questioned how California could realistically enforce such requirements on infinitely forkable open-source software projects. Commercial platforms with proprietary app ecosystems could remain subject to California’s age-assurance requirements even if most open-source Linux distributions are ultimately exempted.
🔗 Read more: https://www.tomshardware.com/software/linux/california-moves-to-exempt-linux-from-its-upcoming-age-verification-law-after-backlash-over-forcing-operating-systems-to-collect-users-ages-amendment-proposed-by-the-same-lawmaker-who-wrote-the-original-law

Alaska's oil revival sparks a new energy rush Into the Arctic
item.description:
📝 Engineers even worried that slow-moving crude would congeal inside the pipeline, creating waxy buildup that could turn TAPS into the world’s biggest tube of ChapStick. “It feels like a bit of the Alaska renaissance,” said ConocoPhillips Chief Executive Officer Ryan Lance. Though the region remains relatively underexplored, recent finds have benefited from companies’ access to oil infrastructure and expertise built over decades at nearby Prudhoe Bay, the Alaska oil field that began pumping crude into TAPS in 1977.
